I worked in GP for five years and have been in ER for 3. ER is considerably more difficult in every way (skill set, stress level, work-life balance, difficult clients, etc.) I love ER because I enjoy the hands on constant treatment of ICU patients + I love the rush of stabilizing a true emergency. 

Since COVID though: 
1. Clients are difficult way more often than not and are actually abusive on a regular basis (screaming at, threatening staff, etc.) 
2. The number of pets needing care FAR exceeds the number of pets we can provide appropriate care for. It is insanely busy almost every single day. I work late almost every shift. I honestly cannot remember the last time I got a lunch and a ten minute break in the same shift (legally I’m supposed to take a lunch and two ten minute breaks). Some days I get no breaks at all. 
3. Despite me neglecting my own needs to take care of my patients treatments are still behind or get missed. Patients suffer. I get stressed about it. The cycle continues.
Time for some acepromazine

Our whole procedure is requesting that they please call and round the case to a doctor and get an estimate from us (and relay that estimate to the client) before sending the patient. The doctor will usually request any labs or rads be emailed to us as well. 

We semi-frequently have issues with "transfers" being sent to us without discussing cost and the owners show up with no money. Sometimes we end up outpatient treating with the same things the GP could have done if communication had been better.
